concept: Calendar prints one month the way a wall sheet does: the days stand flat on the body in a fixed grid, today carries a small index bar under its number, and the day you chose is cut into a small recessed window. Two round keys turn the month.

default_to_avoid.pattern: calendar grid of round buttons where the chosen day is a solid accent-coloured disc and today is a tinted circle
default_to_avoid.why_not: The accent disc spends the unit's one orange on a selection, and today and chosen differ only by tint, so a grey screen or a colour-blind reader cannot tell them apart.

default_to_avoid.pattern: calendar in a floating white card with a drop shadow, dates greyed out as small low-contrast numbers
default_to_avoid.why_not: Greyed numbers fall under 4.5:1 and the floating card adds a second surface, while dial keeps the month on the body of its unit.

references.source: Braun AB 20 quartz alarm clock (Dietrich Lubs, 1975): numerals printed flat on the case with one index mark beside the hour in use
Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): the chosen reading sits in a window cut into the body
WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices, date picker dialog example: grid, roving tabindex and the arrow, Home, End and Page keys

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The chosen day sits in a window that takes surface.sunken and elevation.well with a ring-ink border, so the date you picked reads as the reading and is the only recessed thing in the month.
The chosen day's number turns medium weight while every other day stays regular, so weight tells the choice a second time and a flat copy of the grid still shows it.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: Each day is a 44px square and the two month keys are 44px discs, so the whole month is as easy to hit as the rest of the unit.

derivation.consequence: arrows step a detent, Home and End reach the ends, Space and Enter press
derivation.form: Arrows step a day or a week, Home and End reach the ends of the week, Page keys turn the month, and Space and Enter choose, with one day in the tab order.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: Today, the chosen day and the focus all draw in ink and shape, so a Calendar in a unit never takes the orange away from the unit's primary key.

derivation.consequence: fixed positions, so a unit's layout does not reflow between states
derivation.form: The grid always prints six weeks, with empty cells for days that belong to another month, so turning the month never changes the height of the unit.

options.name: one display window with a solid ink disc and a ring
printed sheet with an index bar and a chosen window

variants.reason: B is printing with one recessed window for the reading, like Stepper and Input, and its index bar and window survive a grey screen; A is a solid disc that reads as a loud round key, and C raises forty-two keys so the month is noisy and the pressed key is hard to find.

root.why: The Calendar shrinks to its own grid so the two keys line up with the edges of the first and last column.

header.why: The month name sits between the two keys on one line, printed on the inset line of the grid below it.

heading.why: The month and year use the emphasis size in medium weight, and it is a live region, so turning the month is read out.

key.why: The previous and next month keys are round 44px keys with a dot-matrix chevron, because they are the only parts that act on the Calendar itself.

grid.why: A table with the grid role, seven columns of 44px, so the cells hold fixed positions and screen readers can walk it by row and column.

weekday.why: The weekday names are small secondary-ink labels printed over the columns, and the full name is read out.

week.why: A row of seven cells, always six rows, so the block size of the month is constant.

cell.why: A 44px cell holds one day or stays empty, so a day keeps the same position under its weekday in every month.

day.why: The day is a button the full size of its cell, so the hit area is 44px; its number is printed flat in tabular figures.

mark.why: A short ink bar under today's number, the same index mark Pagination prints under the current page, so today is a shape and not a tint.

hover.why: Hover darkens a day's ink one step and lifts nothing, because a printed number does not rise when you approach it.

active.why: Pressing a day cuts its recess in at once, with the same well as the chosen day, so the press shows the window that the choice will fill.

focus-visible.why: The focused day, and a focused month key, get the system focus ring offset from the cell, so the roving position is always visible.

data-selected.why: The chosen day gets the recessed window, a ring-ink border and medium weight, which is shape and weight and needs no colour.

data-today.why: Today shows the index bar under its number and is announced with aria-current, so today is told by a shape that still shows when it is also chosen.

data-readonly.why: A read-only Calendar keeps focus and arrow keys but shows a default cursor and no press recess, because nothing can be chosen.

aria-disabled=true.why: A day outside min and max, or one the caller blocks, loses its ink to the disabled step, shows a not-allowed cursor, ignores a press and is announced as unavailable.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under Reduce motion the month keys no longer travel on press and only the ink colour changes.

data-range=inside.why: A day inside a marked range is ruled above and below by a ring-ink hairline, with square corners, so the days between two windows read as one strip by shape and a grey screen still shows the range.

data-preview.why: While the end of a range is still being chosen, the ruled strip is dotted instead of solid, so a range that is only a preview differs from a chosen one by its line and not by a tint.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the chosen day takes the system Highlight pair, days inside a range keep a real border in the text colour, today's bar draws in the text colour and unavailable days use GrayText.

color.why: A day's ink step on hover comes in over the hover duration on the decelerating curve, and nothing else about a day moves.

transform.why: A month key drops by the press travel over the press duration and returns on the release duration, like every secondary key.

box-shadow.why: The month key's shadow collapses under it over the press duration and returns over the release duration, so the drop reads as height going to 0.
